A1.justification: Both complete, readable 27-page PDFs describe the same SemVID research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices can be reliably matched, including the new Appendix D.7 in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original VTG and VideoQA evaluations, token-selection ablations, motion-sensitivity analysis, and inference-latency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds component-level memory and latency measurements in Appendix D.7, Table 11.

M1.justification: Frame-budget allocation and object, motion, and context token selection are unchanged. Appendix B already contains the incremental max-sim MMR implementation in v1; v2 profiles this existing implementation rather than introducing an acceleration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VTG on Charades-STA and ActivityNet-Grounding and VideoQA on Video-MME and LongVideoBench. The new duration-based ActivityNet groups partition existing coverage. Table 10's LVBench-to-LongVideoBench edit clarifies the existing dataset label.

E2.justification: V2 adds a separate overhead comparison in Table 11 against attention-based and similarity-based pruning, discussed as FastV and FastVID in D.7. This adds FastV to efficiency comparisons beyond Table 6's VisionZip/FastVID comparison. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.7 introduces isolated component profiling on equally sized short/long ActivityNet groups defined by duration, measuring latency and pruning-only VRAM excluding raw tokens. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; the no-subtitles statement newly documents an existing Video-MME setting.

E4.justification: Table 11 adds computational analysis separating object selection with and without MMR, motion selection, and context selection across video-length groups. V1 reports aggregate pruning/prefill timing but lacks this breakdown. Existing selection ablations and motion/background sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new profiling table continues reporting point estimates without adding an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds memory and latency results, including object selection with MMR at 16.2/39.9 ms and 2.8/7.6 GB for short/long videos, and attention-based pruning running out of memory on long videos. Existing numerical results in Tables 1–10 and findings in the retained figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16, the attention-graph definitions, ER/CS construction, and Appendix B's MMR complexity argument remain unchanged. D.7 adds an explanatory memory-scaling comparison, without changing the formal framework or supplying a new proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free semantic token allocation, evidence retention and connectivity preservation, and a strong VTG accuracy-efficiency trade-off. The shortened abstract retains the 95.4% mIoU-retention and 5.8× speedup claims; the introduction and conclusion preserve the comparative claims.

C2.justification: D.4 newly interprets the existing VideoQA adaptation as evidence of cross-task robustness through adjusting object/motion priorities. D.7 adds a memory-efficiency explanation contrasting large attention/token-similarity maps with query-patch relevance scores. The existing limitations concerning camera motion and coarse allocation remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access hyperlink in the abstract and explicitly states that Video-MME evaluation excludes subtitles. D.7 documents duration grouping and the VRAM accounting scope. These are added disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a change to the existing implementation or subtitle setting.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al., Revisiting Token Pruning for Object Detection and Instance Segmentation, to the visual-saliency discussion. TokenSculpt's authorship/year entry is updated, but it remains the same cited work and comparator. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 condenses the abstract and selected introductory/method passages, creates a dedicated Section 3, SemVID, for material previously nested under Related Work, and updates author/affiliation information. Most prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 11 and clarifies Table 10's dataset and unpruned-model labels, with revised best-score highlighting. Figures undergo small size/placement adjustments and surrounding text reflows; the existing seven figures and ten tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The new component-level profiling in Table 11 makes the computational costs behind the existing efficiency claim more inspectable. The subtitle disclosure, code-access link, clearer method-section structure, and corrected table labels also improve reproducibility information and readability. These are useful, limited improvements; the main scientific results and method remain stable.
